parts.title: A day on a fishing boat
parts.instructions: Read the article and choose the best answer for each question.
parts.passage:
My uncle Pedro has been a fisherman for thirty years, and last summer he finally agreed to take me out on his boat. We left the harbour at four in the morning, when the sky was still dark and the town was asleep. I was so sleepy that I almost fell into the water as I climbed on board.

The first hour was peaceful. Pedro steered the boat with one hand and drank coffee from a metal cup, while I watched the sun rise over the sea. Then he stopped the engine and told me to help him pull in the nets. It was much harder than it looked. The ropes were wet and heavy, and my hands were soon red and sore.

At first, I was disappointed because the nets seemed almost empty. 'Be patient,' said Pedro. Then I saw hundreds of silver fish jumping inside them. We worked for another hour to sort them into boxes. Pedro explained which ones were good to sell and which ones we should return to the sea.

By noon, I was exhausted but proud. That evening, my aunt cooked some of our fish for dinner, and it was the best meal I have ever eaten. I have decided to go out with Pedro every summer, although perhaps I will go to bed earlier the night before.

questions.prompt: How did the writer feel when they left the harbour?
questions.explanation: He was so sleepy that he almost fell into the water.

options: Steering the boat in the dark
Making the coffee for his uncle
questions.explanation: Pulling in the nets was much harder than it looked.

questions.prompt: Why was the writer disappointed at first?
options: The weather was far too cold
The boat was moving very slowly
questions.explanation: The nets seemed almost empty.

questions.prompt: What did Pedro explain?
options: Where the best places to fish were
How to repair a torn net quickly
Which fish to sell and which to return
questions.explanation: He explained which fish were good to sell and which to return to the sea.

questions.prompt: What does the writer plan to do?
options: Buy his own small boat soon
questions.explanation: He has decided to go out with Pedro every summer.

parts.title: My first sailing lesson
parts.instructions: Choose the sentence that fits each gap. There is one extra sentence.
parts.passage:
I had never been in a sailing boat before, so I felt nervous when I arrived at the club on Saturday morning. [1] Our instructor, a cheerful woman called Marta, welcomed us and gave us all life jackets.

First, she showed us the different parts of the boat on land. [2] I tried to remember the names, but there were so many that my head began to spin. After half an hour, we were finally allowed to go onto the water.

The wind was light, and our little boat moved slowly across the lake. [3] Marta sat beside me and told me when to move the sail. Suddenly, a strong gust arrived, and the boat leaned so far that I was sure we would fall in. [4] Marta laughed and told me to keep calm, and soon we were sailing straight again.

By the end of the lesson, I was soaking wet but extremely happy. [5] I have already booked another lesson for next weekend.
sentences: I held the rope in one hand and the steering stick in the other.
Sailing is much more expensive than most people think.
There were about ten other beginners, and none of us knew what to do.
I had never felt so free.
My heart was beating like a drum.
Some of them had strange names, like boom and rudder.

gaps.explanation: Ten other beginners explains why she was nervous, and "our instructor" then welcomes them.
"Some of them" refers to the parts of the boat, whose names she tried to remember.
Holding the rope and the steering stick describes what she did as the boat moved.
Her heart beating like a drum fits the frightening moment when the boat leaned.
"I had never felt so free" explains why she was happy and wanted another lesson.

parts.title: A postcard from the coast

parts.passage: Dear Ruth, We [1] a lovely time here by the sea since Monday. The weather has been perfect, so we have [2] most of the time on the beach. Yesterday, I went out in a small boat for the first time. At first, I was afraid [3] falling in, but then I relaxed and enjoyed it. This morning, we [4] some shells to take home. It is a pity that we [5] home tomorrow. Next summer, I would like to come [6] with you.

questions.explanation: "Since Monday" needs the present perfect continuous.

questions.prompt: Gap 2

parts.title: Boat safety rules
parts.instructions: Write one word in each gap.
parts.passage: Welcome aboard! Please read these safety rules carefully before we leave the harbour. Everyone [1] wear a life jacket at all times, even if the sea looks calm. Do not stand up [2] the boat is moving, because the floor can be wet. Please keep your hands inside the boat, [3] you could hurt yourself badly. Children must stay [4] an adult during the whole trip. If you feel ill, tell a crew member [5] once and sit down. We hope [6] enjoy your trip with us today!

gaps.explanation: A rule about safety needs "must" or "should".
"While" refers to the time when the boat is moving.
"Or" explains what could happen if you do not follow the rule.
The crew hope that "you" will enjoy the trip.

parts.title: A boat trip along the coast
parts.instructions: Listen to the talk and complete each note with one word.

turns.speaker: rhys
turns.text: Good morning, everybody, and welcome aboard the Seagull. I'm Captain Rhys. Today's trip lasts two hours, and we're going to sail along the coast as far as the Red Rocks. Please stay seated while the boat is moving. The life jackets are under your seats, in case you need them. On the left, you can see Seal Island, where about fifty seals live. If we are lucky, we may also see dolphins. There is a small shop on board that sells hot drinks and sandwiches. A cup of tea costs three pounds. We will arrive back in the harbour at noon. Finally, please don't throw any rubbish into the sea. Thank you, and enjoy the trip.

gaps.explanation: They will sail as far as the Red Rocks.
The life jackets are under the seats.

gaps.explanation: About fifty seals live on Seal Island.

gaps.prompt: A cup of tea costs ___ pounds
gaps.explanation: A cup of tea costs three pounds.

gaps.prompt: The boat returns to the harbour at ___
gaps.explanation: They arrive back in the harbour at noon.

parts.title: A sailor
parts.instructions: Listen to the interview and choose the correct answer.

turns.speaker: gerard
turns.text: My guest today is Jenna Marsh, who sailed across the Atlantic alone in a small boat. Jenna, how long did the crossing take?

turns.speaker: jenna
turns.text: Forty days. I had planned for thirty-five, but the wind dropped for a week, and I hardly moved at all.

turns.speaker: gerard
turns.text: What was the hardest part?

turns.speaker: jenna
turns.text: Sleeping. You cannot sleep for eight hours when you are alone at sea, so I slept for twenty minutes at a time, and I was always tired.

turns.speaker: gerard
turns.text: Were you ever frightened?

turns.speaker: jenna
turns.text: Once, in a storm. The waves were as high as a house, and I stayed below deck, holding on for hours. I kept telling myself that the boat was stronger than I was.

turns.speaker: gerard
turns.text: What was your best moment?

turns.speaker: jenna
turns.text: Dolphins. They swam beside the boat for an entire afternoon, and I was not alone any more. I talked to them for hours.

turns.speaker: gerard
turns.text: What did you eat?

turns.speaker: jenna
turns.text: Mostly tinned food and rice. By the end, I would have given anything for a fresh apple.

turns.speaker: gerard
turns.text: What will you do next?

turns.speaker: jenna
turns.text: I'm planning to sail round the world, and this time my daughter is coming with me.
